summary: Intermittent streaming stalls when large tracing headers are fragmented by LB causing prolonged idle before ALB reset
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on dedicated clusters observe long-running streaming completions enter a silent period (no bytes) for ~30–90s and then the ALB connection is closed with a 504/stream-reset. This primarily happens when large tracing/debug headers are present (client libraries that append verbose trace context or long cookie blobs).

Impact:
- BrightCart observed 12% of streaming requests for their checkout assistant experience a mid-stream silence longer than 30s, producing user-visible stalls and retries.
- Affects production traffic in us-east on dedicated cluster pool BRIGHT-DC-3.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: BRIGHT-DC-3 (prod, us-east)
- API path: /v1/streams/generate (http2 fronted by ALB -> API gateway -> envoy proxy -> serving runtime)
- Client: BrightCart backend using okhttp/Java HTTP/2 with instrumentation that attaches large X-Bright-Trace headers (~18–25KB).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client opens HTTP/2 streaming request with multiple tracing headers (X-Bright-Trace, X-Session-Meta) totaling >16KB.
2) Server accepts and begins token emission; first chunk(s) stream normally for ~2–5s while KV-cache warms.
3) Mid-stream the HTTP/2 connection shows zero bytes forwarded for ~30–90s. No application logs show backlog; runtime reports tokens emitted to socket but ALB side stalls until ALB RST/timeout.

Observed behavior / logs excerpt:
- ALB access: target_status=504, elb_status=200, request_processing_time=0.003, backend_processing_time=35.642, response_processing_time=0.000
- Envoy metrics: downstream_rq_active: spikes at time of stall; upstream tx bytes stop but upstream code reports generated tokens.
- Tcpdump (target): sequence shows header CONTINUATION frames interleaved with data frames; last frame seen from target was a small DATA frame at t=+4s; client-side sees no data after that and ALB sends RST at t=+39s.

Investigation notes:
- SRE captured an HTTP/2 trace: large headers are split across HEADERS + CONTINUATION frames (HPACK). ALB/edge sometimes moves the connection to a different worker when CONTINUATION frames arrive and TCP segmentation plus internal write coalescing delays flushing.
- Kernel-level TCP coalescing + our envoy proxy's proxy_buffering setting appears to wait for a flush boundary; when header CONTINUATION frames interleave with mid-stream DATA frames, ALB's idle detection doesn't see expected byte flow and triggers a backend idle timeout.
- We reproduced locally by sending a streaming request with artificially large header block and observed the same behavior when the request was proxied through an ALB configured with HTTP/2 + proxy buffering.

Hypothesis:
- Combination of large HPACK-encoded headers (many CONTINUATION frames) and our proxy/ALB buffering causes intermittent pauses in the observed data plane. ALB expects regular DATA frames but header-related frame interleaving plus socket-level coalescing can prevent timely flushes, tripping the ALB idle timeout. The issue is amplified on dedicated nodes where client libraries add verbose trace metadata.

Temporary workarounds for customer (applied):
- BrightCart removed the verbose X-Bright-Trace payload for critical streaming routes (reduced header size <4KB) — immediate reduction in stall rate.
- Support created a dedicated routing rule to pin traffic to a path with keepalive and reduced proxy_buffering for BRIGHT-DC-3 (stopgap).

Action items / next steps:
- Short term: Add a routing flag to disable header coalescing/proxy_buffering for streaming routes during edge/proxy hop (SRE task).
- Medium term: Coordinate with infra to tune ALB idle thresholds for dedicated pools and verify behavior when HPACK CONTINUATION frames are present.
- Long term: Add an agent/SDK best-practice doc advising customers to avoid huge per-request tracing headers on streaming endpoints; consider server-side truncation metrics and warnings in Console.

Resolution notes:
Investigation ongoing. Customer workaround applied and confirmed to reduce incidents. Engineering owning: network & proxy team (Aisha Ramos).
investigation_notes: Captured tcpdump and envoy traces show HPACK CONTINUATION frames mixed with DATA frames. Local repro with okhttp stream + artificial 20KB header produced identical stub: mid-stream silence then ALB reset. No evidence of serving runtime stalling; tokens generate into socket. Hypothesis points to proxy/ALB buffering + http2 frame fragmentation edge-case.
hypothesis: ALB/internal proxy buffering combined with HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame ordering and kernel write coalescing can delay flushes long enough to trip ALB idle timeout for long-lived streaming requests when large headers are present.
workaround: 1) Reduce header payloads (<4KB) for streaming endpoints. 2) Route affected clients to a pinned upstream with proxy_buffering disabled. 3) Increase ALB backend idle timeout on dedicated pools temporarily.
resolution_plan: Implement routing flag to disable header coalescing for streaming routes (SRE ticket). Tune ALB idle timeout for dedicated pools and publish SDK guidance for trace header limits.
